title: Permission model
subtitle: rwx, octal modes, special bits, and ext attributes — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Owner UID, group GID, and mode bits
cards.notes: Who = owner / group / world. What = r w x.

cards.meaning: type + user rwx + group rwx + other rwx, then owner, group, size, name
cards.notes: Type: - file, d directory, l symlink, c/b device.

cards.meaning: Linux checks one bucket: owner, else group, else other — not the union
cards.notes: From theory-study: not the union of all three.

cards.meaning: Open / read contents
Modify contents
Run as a program or script
List names (ls)
Create, delete, or rename entries (also needs x)
cards.notes: Directory w without x cannot create or delete names.

cards.meaning: Enter / resolve a path (cd, open a file inside)
cards.notes: Directory x = “may walk into.” Without x you cannot cd or open a path through it, even with r.

cards.meaning: A directory operation (unlink) — directory write controls it, not the file’s own mode
cards.notes: Without sticky bit, write on the directory is enough to delete anyone’s file inside.

cards.meaning: Set the user (owner) of the path
cards.notes: chown = user owner. Only root can give a file to another user on typical Linux.

cards.meaning: Set owner and group together
Change ownership recursively
Set the group owner of a path
cards.notes: chgrp = group owner.

cards.meaning: Change group ownership recursively

cards.notes: Memory hook: 4-2-1. Three digits = user, group, other.

cards.meaning: rwxr-xr-x — executable or directory others may enter
rw-r--r-- — typical normal file
rwx------ — private to owner
rwxrwxrwx — everyone everything; avoid except /tmp with sticky bit
Set mode by numbers when you think in octal
cards.notes: chmod 755 when you think in numbers; chmod g+w when you think in letters.

cards.meaning: Set group bits exactly to read+write (clears group x)
cards.notes: = sets that class exactly.

cards.meaning: Take read from other, add write to group
cards.notes: Who: u g o a. Operators: + add, - remove, = exact.

cards.meaning: Add execute for u/g/o that already make sense
u=user, g=group, o=other, a=all
On a shared directory: only the file owner (or root) may delete/rename an entry
cards.example: bob’s /tmp/bob is safe from tom even if /tmp is 777
cards.notes: Used mainly on /tmp and /var/tmp. Memory hook: you may only throw away your trash.

cards.meaning: Sticky bit shown in other’s execute slot; capital means sticky on and execute off
cards.notes: s/S and t/T: capital = special bit on AND execute off.

cards.meaning: Set sticky bit on a directory
Leading 1 = sticky + 700
cards.notes: Octal extra digit 1 = sticky.

cards.meaning: Remove sticky bit
Leading 0 = no SUID/SGID/sticky + 700
Process effective UID becomes the file owner when you run it
cards.example: passwd binary runs as root to update /etc/shadow
cards.notes: Linux typically ignores SUID on scripts — it applies to binaries.

cards.meaning: Leading 4 = SUID
Process effective GID becomes the file’s group; on a directory, new files inherit that group
cards.notes: Keeps a shared project tree in one group instead of creator’s primary GID.

cards.meaning: Leading 2 = SGID
4 = SUID, 2 = SGID, 1 = sticky
cards.notes: Memory hook: extra octal 4 / 2 / 1.

cards.meaning: Sticky + world rwx — typical /tmp mode
List ext filesystem attributes (beyond rwx)
cards.notes: chmod = rwx. chattr = extra ext flags. lsattr to see them.

cards.meaning: List attributes recursively
Treat directory as a file — show the directory itself, not its contents
Immutable — no edit, delete, or rename until unlocked with -i
cards.notes: i = frozen. Unlock before you edit.

cards.meaning: No atime — access does not update last-access time
cards.notes: Less inode churn on hot read files.

cards.meaning: Append-only — file: only append; directory: add files but not rename/delete existing ones
cards.notes: a = append only.

cards.meaning: Secure deletion — on delete, zero the blocks (like shred)
cards.notes: Not all filesystems honor this.
